title: Global EV Sales Volume and Share by Region, 2020–2025
executive_question: How fast has global EV adoption grown across major regions, and where is growth accelerating or slowing?
required_metrics: Annual global EV sales volume (million units), 2020–2025
Annual EV sales volume by region (China, Europe, North America, Rest of World), 2020–2025
Annual EV share of total new vehicle sales by region (%), 2020–2025
comparison_set: China vs Europe vs North America vs Rest of World
search_queries: IEA Global EV Outlook annual EV sales by region 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025
China Europe North America annual electric vehicle sales volume 2020-2025 official
global EV share of new car sales by region annual data 2020-2025
data_quality_rule: Use at least four same-basis annual observations per region. If only two endpoints are available, derive intermediate years using a transparent CAGR or public forecast benchmark, label them as estimates, and never present two endpoints as a trend line.
narrative_role: Establishes the baseline growth trajectory and regional divergence that frames the competitive race.
pre_exhibit_context: The report opens with the claim that EV growth is no longer a single global curve but a set of regionally distinct adoption paths.
post_exhibit_takeaway: China remains the volume engine, Europe is consolidating, and North America is policy-sensitive; the next phase is about share defense, not just market creation.

title: Global EV Market Revenue and Average Selling Price, 2020–2025
executive_question: Is market value growing in line with volume, or are price declines compressing revenue growth?
required_metrics: Annual global EV market revenue (USD billion), 2020–2025
Annual average EV selling price by region (USD/unit), 2020–2025
Annual EV revenue by region (USD billion), 2020–2025
comparison_set: Global vs China vs Europe vs North America
preferred_sources: Company annual reports (Tesla, BYD, Volkswagen, GM, Ford)
search_queries: global electric vehicle market revenue annual 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 USD billion
average electric vehicle selling price by region annual 2020-2025
EV revenue by region annual data IEA BloombergNEF 2020-2025
data_quality_rule: Use at least four same-basis annual observations. If revenue is not directly reported, calculate from unit sales and ASP, mark calculated years as estimates, and disclose the estimation rule.
narrative_role: Tests whether volume growth translates into revenue growth and sets up the margin pressure argument.
pre_exhibit_context: The section argues that EV competition is shifting from volume expansion to value capture as prices fall.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Revenue growth is slower than unit growth in several regions, meaning scale alone no longer guarantees profit pool expansion.

title: EV Competitive Position Bubble Map: Volume, Growth, and Profitability
executive_question: Which automakers combine scale, growth, and profitability, and who is vulnerable to a shakeout?
required_metrics: Annual EV unit sales by automaker (thousand units), latest fiscal year
Year-over-year EV unit sales growth by automaker (%), latest fiscal year
EV segment operating margin or automotive gross margin by automaker (%), latest fiscal year
comparison_set: BYD, Tesla, Volkswagen Group, SAIC, Geely, Hyundai-Kia, GM, Ford, Stellantis, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto
search_queries: automaker annual EV unit sales 2024 2025 BYD Tesla Volkswagen SAIC Geely
EV segment operating margin by automaker annual report 2024 2025
global EV market share by automaker annual 2024 2025 S&P Global Mobility
data_quality_rule: Use reported unit sales and margins where available. If EV-specific margin is not disclosed, use automotive segment margin and label it as a proxy. Do not mix fiscal years without disclosure.
narrative_role: Maps the competitive landscape beyond unit sales to reveal which players can sustain investment.
pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that the EV race is separating into scale leaders, profit-funded challengers, and loss-making laggards.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Only a small group combines high volume, positive growth, and positive EV margins; most others face strategic dependency on external funding or legacy profits.

title: Global EV Battery Demand and Manufacturing Capacity, 2020–2025
executive_question: Is battery supply keeping pace with EV demand, and where is overcapacity or shortage emerging?
required_metrics: Annual global EV battery demand (GWh), 2020–2025
Annual global EV battery manufacturing capacity (GWh), 2020–2025
Annual battery demand and capacity by region (China, Europe, North America), 2020–2025
comparison_set: Demand vs capacity; China vs Europe vs North America
preferred_sources: Company annual reports (CATL, LG Energy Solution, Panasonic, BYD)
search_queries: global EV battery demand GWh annual 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 IEA
global EV battery manufacturing capacity GWh by region annual 2020-2025
SNE Research battery demand capacity annual 2024 2025
data_quality_rule: Use same-basis annual demand and capacity data. If capacity is announced rather than operational, label as announced capacity and distinguish from utilized capacity.
narrative_role: Connects upstream supply chain capacity to downstream competitive dynamics and cost trends.
pre_exhibit_context: The section argues that battery supply is no longer the binding constraint, shifting competition to cost and technology.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Battery capacity has grown faster than demand in several regions, pressuring cell prices and forcing consolidation among suppliers.

title: EV Policy and Regulatory Milestones by Major Market, 2020–2030
executive_question: Which regulatory deadlines and incentives will force or delay EV adoption in the largest markets?
required_metrics: Policy name and jurisdiction
Effective date or target year
Quantitative target or penalty (e.g., CO2 g/km, NEV credit %, subsidy amount USD/vehicle)
comparison_set: China vs European Union vs United States vs India vs Japan
preferred_sources: China Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT)
search_queries: EU CO2 emission standards passenger cars 2025 2030 2035 official
China NEV mandate credit percentage 2024 2025 MIIT
US EPA vehicle emissions rules 2027 2032 IRA EV tax credit official
data_quality_rule: Use official government or regulator sources. Include effective dates and quantitative targets. Do not include proposed rules without labeling them as proposed.
narrative_role: Shows that competition is shaped by policy clocks, not just consumer demand.
pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that the next five years of EV competition will be determined by regulatory gates and subsidy transitions.
post_exhibit_takeaway: China’s NEV mandate, Europe’s CO2 targets and 2035 ICE ban, and US IRA/EPA rules create different timing risks and opportunities for automakers.

title: EV Charging Infrastructure Deployment vs EV Fleet, 2020–2025
executive_question: Is charging infrastructure keeping pace with EV adoption, and where is the infrastructure gap largest?
required_metrics: Annual public EV charging points by region (thousand units), 2020–2025
Annual EV fleet by region (million units), 2020–2025
Charging points per 100 EVs by region, 2020–2025
comparison_set: China vs Europe vs United States
preferred_sources: China Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Promotion Alliance (EVCIPA)
US Department of Energy Alternative Fuels Data Center
search_queries: global public EV charging points annual by region 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 IEA
China public charging piles annual 2020-2025 EVCIPA
US public EV chargers annual 2020-2025 Department of Energy
data_quality_rule: Use same-basis annual counts for public charging points and EV fleet. If data definitions differ (public vs private, slow vs fast), disclose and do not aggregate without adjustment.
narrative_role: Tests whether adoption is constrained by charging availability and identifies infrastructure investment opportunities.
pre_exhibit_context: The report argues that charging availability is becoming a competitive differentiator and a bottleneck in some regions.
post_exhibit_takeaway: China leads in absolute charger deployment but still faces utilization and grid issues; Europe and the US have larger gaps per EV, creating investment needs.

title: EV Cost Parity and Total Cost of Ownership by Segment, 2020–2025
executive_question: When and where do EVs reach cost parity with internal combustion vehicles, and how does that vary by segment?
required_metrics: Annual average EV purchase price by segment (USD/unit), 2020–2025
Annual average ICE purchase price by segment (USD/unit), 2020–2025
Annual total cost of ownership for EV vs ICE by segment (USD/mile or USD/year), 2020–2025
comparison_set: EV vs ICE; compact vs mid-size vs SUV vs truck; China vs Europe vs US
search_queries: EV vs ICE purchase price by segment annual 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025
total cost of ownership EV vs ICE by segment annual 2020-2025 ICCT
China Europe US EV price parity segment annual data 2020-2025
data_quality_rule: Use at least four same-basis annual observations per segment. If TCO is not directly reported, calculate from purchase price, fuel/electricity cost, maintenance, and resale value, and label calculated years as estimates.
narrative_role: Quantifies the economic driver behind adoption and shows where parity is already achieved or still distant.
pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that cost parity is the single most important demand trigger, but it is arriving at different speeds by segment and region.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Compact and mid-size EVs in China and Europe are near or at parity, while large SUVs and trucks in the US remain dependent on subsidies or premium pricing.
